Put sources onto a common one-second clock

Source: R/align.R
align_rides.Rd

Two meters recording the same ride do not necessarily agree about what time it is. When each records to its own head unit the clocks can differ by several seconds, and differencing the series on nominal timestamps then compares power from one moment against power from another. That inflates the spread, shifts the bias, and looks entirely plausible on the way out.

Usage

align_rides(rides, max_offset = 30)

alignment_report(aligned)

Arguments

rides

Long tibble from read_rides().

max_offset

Largest offset to consider, in seconds. Set to 0 to trust the recorded timestamps and skip estimation.

aligned

Result of align_rides().

Value

A tibble of run, source, t (seconds from the start of the run), time and the ride channels, with an alignment report attached. Retrieve the report with alignment_report().

Details

Within each run every source is resampled onto a one-second grid, then the offset against a reference source is estimated by maximising the cross-correlation of the power series. Where both channels came from a single head unit the estimate is zero, so the same path serves both cases. Gaps left by pauses or smart recording stay NA rather than being interpolated across.

Examples

aligned <- read_rides(demo_rides()) |> align_rides()

# The demo plants a seven-second offset on one meter, and it comes back
alignment_report(aligned)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   run   source  reference offset correlation sharpness status 
#>   <chr> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1 run1  assioma assioma        0      NA        NA     assumed
#> 2 run1  kickr   assioma        7       0.996     0.113 aligned
#> 3 run2  assioma assioma        0      NA        NA     assumed
#> 4 run2  quarq   assioma        0       0.997     0.135 aligned
